q4-goals.name: Shop goals - Q4 2026
q4-goals.content:
# Shop goals, Q4 2026

Written by Dan, Oct 1. Looked at in the Monday crew meeting.

We had our best September ever ($41k collected) but we are turning down work and the office is me at 9pm. Q4 is about getting the second journeyman, getting paid faster, and turning one-off customers into repeat customers.

## Goals

| # | Goal | Target | Owner | How we track it |
|---|------|--------|-------|-----------------|
| 1 | Hire a second journeyman | Start date by Dec 15 | Dan | TradeHire listing, interviews |
| 2 | Launch the yearly drain maintenance plan | 25 signups by Dec 31 | | Dispatchly recurring jobs |
| 3 | No invoice over 30 days | $0 over 30 days by Nov 30 | Dan + Joan | LedgerNest overdue report |
| 4 | Amy backflow certified | Pass the December exam | Amy (shop pays the $185) | Exam registration |
| 5 | Keep Google rating at 4.6 or better | Reply to every review within 24 hours | Dan | Google Business Profile |
| 6 | Win the Lakeshore Building C toilet job | Signed by Dec 15, about $11k | Kevin quotes, Dan sends | Lakeshore project |

## Goal 2: drain maintenance plan

What it is: $149 a year. Includes one kitchen or main-line drain cleaning, one water heater flush, a visual check of shutoffs and supply lines, and 10% off any repair for the year. We price it so the drain cleaning alone ($219 normally) is cheaper than paying for it once.

Why: we have about 140 customers who have called us twice or more since 2024. If 25 sign up that's $3,725 up front and two booked visits each in our slow months (January, February, July).

What has to happen before we can sell it (nobody has started this):

- Set it up as a recurring job type in Dispatchly with a reminder 2 weeks before the visit.
- One-page flyer techs leave behind, and a line on every invoice.
- Decide who gets asked first: Sandra Whitlock asked about it last spring and again in October.
- Card on file through Tillpoint for the annual charge.

## Goal 3 notes

Joan sends the LedgerNest overdue list on the 1st and 15th. Automatic reminders are off because I didn't like the default wording.

## Parking lot

- Van wraps (WrapKing quote): not this year.
- Second truck for drain work: revisit when the journeyman starts.

# Price book 2026

Use these numbers on the phone and on site. If a job isn't here, call Dan before you quote. Updated Sep 15, 2026.

## Service calls

- Trip charge: $89. **Tell the customer on the phone, every time.** Waived if the job is over $300. If they cancel at the door, the trip charge still applies.
- Hourly labor: $135 per hour after the first hour, billed in half hours.
- After-hours and weekend call-out: $225 (includes the first hour), then $165 per hour.
- Arrival windows: 2 hours. Text the customer when you leave the previous job.

## Drains

- Kitchen or bathroom drain cleaning (cable): $219
- Main line cleaning from a cleanout: $349. No cleanout: add $150.
- Sewer camera inspection: $295, or $150 when done with a cleaning
- Hydro-jetting (commercial): $650 for the first 2 hours

## Water heaters

- Flush and anode check: $175; anode replacement adds $70 (parts included)
- 40 gal gas, installed with permit and haul-away: $2,180
- 50 gal gas, installed with permit and haul-away: $2,450

## Fixtures

- $149 per year. See Shop goals, goal 2.

# Crew handbook (DRAFT)

Started by Dan, Sep 28. I need this done before the new journeyman starts so I'm not explaining it differently to everybody.

## 1. Hours and pay

- Normal day 7:30 to 4:00, first job at 8:00. Shop days are 8 to 4:30.
- Pay is weekly, Friday. Timesheets due Friday 5pm for the week (Monday to Friday) plus any on-call hours.
- Overtime is time and a half over 40 hours in the week. Tell Dan before a job is going to run past 6pm.
- Mileage is logged per van in the van log, not on your timesheet.

## 2. Pay rates and ranges (posted on TradeHire)

- Journeyman plumber: $32 to $38 per hour depending on experience and license.
- Apprentice: $19 to $22 per hour. Raises at each completed year of the apprenticeship.
- On-call stipend: TODO

TODO: how many weekends a month, who is in the rotation (Luis, Kevin, Tyrell, new hire?), what counts as an emergency, call-back time, how on-call hours get paid, what happens on holidays (Thanksgiving, Christmas).

permit-process.name: How we handle permits & inspections
permit-process.content:
# How we handle permits and inspections (City of Brennerton)

Contractor license P-11842. Portal login: Dan (shared login is in the office binder, not here).

## When we need a permit

- Water heater replacement (gas or electric): yes, over-the-counter, usually 1 to 2 business days.
- Repipe, new fixtures in new locations, gas line work, sewer line replacement: yes.
- Like-for-like toilet, faucet or disposal swaps: no.
- Backflow tests: no permit, but the report goes to the city's cross-connection program.

## Steps

1. **Apply.** Dan applies in the portal. For repipes, attach a riser or isometric diagram, the fixture count per floor and the signed owner authorization. Missing items mean resubmittal (that cost us a week on PB-26-03544).
2. **Post the permit card** at the site before any work starts.
3. **Rough-in inspection.** For anything going inside walls, the rough-in (with pressure test) has to pass before walls are closed. Request it in the portal at least 24 hours ahead. The lead tech on the job tells Dan the date the day the job starts; Dan requests it.
4. **Final inspection.** Request when fixtures are connected. Someone has to be there to give access (the customer doesn't need to be home if we are).
5. **Close out.** Passed final = permit closed. Save the inspection record PDF to the customer's folder and note it on the invoice.

## If the walls get closed before rough-in

The inspector can make the owner open the walls. That's on us, not the customer. It happened once in 2024 (Delmar job): $1,400 of drywall we paid for.

## Timelines

- Permit expires 180 days after it's issued if work hasn't started.
- Applications incomplete after 30 days are withdrawn.
- Inspection windows are 8 to 12 or 12 to 4. The inspector usually calls 30 minutes ahead.

retro-building-c.name: Retro: Building C emergency (Oct 30)
retro-building-c.content:
# Retro: Building C main service line break, Oct 30

Written by Luis, Nov 1.

## What happened

Brian called at 6:45am: no water to Building C (24 units), water bubbling up in the parking strip by the meter. The utility had shut it off at the street. Kevin and I were on site by 8:00 with Amy following. We rented an excavator ($640, half day), found the break right at the curb stop on the customer side, replaced 12 ft of 1" type K copper with two compression couplings, and had water back on at 4:40pm. The curb stop itself is the utility's side and wasn't replaced. Brian authorized up to $8,000; the final came in at $4,870.

## What went well

- Two techs on site within 75 minutes of the call.
- Amy ran the locator and did the compression fittings with me. She's ready for more of this.
- Tenants back on water by dinner, nobody put in a hotel. Brian brought pizza.
- Photos taken at every step and put in the shared folder.

## What didn't go well

- The invoice went out as one line. Lakeshore's AP needs it split: the emergency repair under WO-5551, the excavator rental as its own line with the receipt.
- The rental receipt was in my truck for three days.
- The photos were in the shared folder but not attached to the invoice.
- Tyrell and Amy's morning jobs got bumped and two customers weren't called until noon.

## What we'll do next time

| Action | Owner | Status |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Invoice template with one line per work order and a rental line | Dan | Not started |
| Rental receipts photographed and texted to Dan same day | Whoever rents | Agreed |
| When an emergency bumps jobs, office calls bumped customers within 1 hour | Dan | Agreed |
| Keep a half-day excavator rental contact in the van binder | Luis | Done |
